title: Fun at first, but needs improving
body: This game was fun at first, the storyline is typical reborn and revenge and goes very very slowly (too slow to be honest, speaking from almost level 30). The biggest problem is once you pass level 20, the amount of energy given as the default is not enough to keep a player engaged. You either have to spend ruby, or wait, or watch ad, or spend real money, most players will choose to wait and will eventually lose patience then quit the game. If you want feedback, give more surveys with big big rewards, or give one reward to a one question quick voluntary survey, you as developers should be able to tell if a player just quickly glanced through the survey or if a player took their time to consider answers. In addition, you should consider increase energy default to 150/200/250/300/350 and so on as a player advances through levels, that way less people will uninstall the game. Also, give more options to decorate through leveling up, instead of auto decors, and give the option to go back to change decors, as perhaps rewards. Also, the amount of coins needed to advance the story is too random and does not necessarily correlate with story hidden behind the chapter name. Why not make it consistently?? Are you suggesting certain chapters are more important/interesting hence requires more coins? That’s confusing. You should look to candy crush and how successful that game was and their principles to keep players engaged. Also, let the main characters change outfits as an option for A DAY as a holiday or special valentine’s day would be fun. Lastly, what’s the point of that cat task if it is almost impossible to complete it without spending real money, that just make players give up and get frustrated seeing it everyday, give the option to clear or delete a task they don’t want to complete. If you want more players, give friend referral reward codes!

title: Money Drain
body: This is legit my favorite game. It’s beautiful, the story is engaging, the characters are fun. I love the decorating elements and new home and fashion aspects. BUT this game has become predatory. I started being able to view ads for additional energy. Then they were reduced. Then removed entirely. You don’t get more energy allotments or skills as you level up, just one off rewards. In discussion with other players, there appears to be an algorithm that either tracks how much you play, spend, and/or view ads, and then recalibrates accordingly to your gameplay. This is unconfirmed, obviously, but it feels super plausible. I want to keep playing, but would love to play for more than 2 minutes at a time because 1 item drains 700 energy and you only get 100 every 3 hours. I don’t mind spending some money, especially on one as gorgeous and fun as this. But at this rate, either make it a straight up paid game or subscription, but at least make it playable without an arm and a leg and all your ancestors’ jade.

title: Entertaining and Relaxing, but…
body: I’ve been playing for about a week now, and I can say that it’s actually pretty enjoyable. The energy cap isn’t that bad, and with the new update letting us watch ads to get energy, I can’t complain. It’s easy to get to higher levels, and the UI isn’t hard to interact with. The story is a bit on the cliche side, being a pretty standard ‘back in time, I’ll change my life, girl boss’ kind of story, but it hits enough of the satisfying story marks without being so annoying, that I don’t actually have many complaints. The reward system feels fair, and all the currency, even the gems, are not too hard to get. However, despite all that, I can still only give it three stars. One, is for the micro transactions that are just permanently clogging up the right side of the screen. I get that some of the stuff is for events, but if there was a way to make it like a menu that can retract or such, that would make the game feel more leisurely. This is also including the packs that keep popping up when you open the game. Second, is my biggest complain, and it’s the use of AI in all the visuals. The game itself is fun, but all of the AI really pulls me out of it. Nothing is really consistent style wise, and it’s so off-putting for something that’s meant to feel like a traditional teahouse. Looking at Softy doesn’t make me feel like he’s a majestic being, or even cute, he’s just a strange, texture-less thing AI styled thing. And when you look at all the items together, all the quality of everything is so different from each other. I don’t know how long this game has been out, but I think it deserves a visual update. Even though I don’t condone the use of AI in the use of the arts in any way, since it’s already in use, why not use it as just a placeholder, and get actual artists to design more consistent items, and characters with what’s already there as references? It doesn’t need to be a mass thing, I understand that takes a lot of time, and money, but even just some items at a time, like the statues, and other unchangeable items. I’m sure many other players would be much happier for a more cohesive personal style, than something that feels churned out. This review is getting pretty long, so I’ll stop here, but devs, I do hope you’ll consider these suggestions.

title: How to make it better....
body: I've played this game for a while now. I'm actually level 23 and here's some feedback that I have to make the game less frustrating. Consider replenishing the health meter every time one levels up, especially as you get higher in levels the requests for items are a higher version and it can take literally all 100 heath points to get to maybe the level BEFORE the actual requested item. That's the most frustrating part. Being out of health because the game tops off at 100. I suggest once an individual reaches level 20 to increase the health meter to 200. The start of the game, the backstory went by so fast I had no idea what was happening. The text flew by along with the cut scenes so I had little understanding as to what had even happened. The servant name keeps ping ponging back and forth between Ryen and Zea....pick a lane already!! There's this special item that allows one to use the items without having to wait for them to recharge for a specific time period. However, that item is automatically put into effect rather than allowing us to use it when it benefits us. We earned the special item and yet we have no choice when we want to use it. Sometimes I want to play a quick round and that item suddenly goes into effect and I lose out on it because I need to exit the game because I need to board my flight! The art is fantastic and I love the stills of cut scenes. I keep playing because the art is so beautiful and the story is actually engaging. Sometimes the text is a bit confusing. They should be saying "my lady" not "my miss" which sounds weird and a poor translation. I will say that this game is basically a carbon copy of Gossip Harbor in terms of game play. Even down to the advertisement for it, which has ZERO correlation to the actual game. What is with these games providing false advertising???!!!! I deleted gossip harbor because I got bored with it and how frustrating it got to complete the requests. And I didn't quite like the story line as much. I'm only sticking it out with this game for the art and story....but the more frustrating it gets....the higher the chances I'll delete it too. If the game is able to provide these improvements, I fully believe the game will be more engaging. I have one other merge game that I've kept up with: Longleaf Valley. It has its frustrating points, but for the most part it's fair in game advancement. Consider testing them out for ideas.

title: After 9 days of gameplay
body: I have played this game daily since I downloaded it, with a couple hours each day. For context, I'm on level/chapter 28 in the story, so I feel I've progressed enough to share my thoughts. There are great parts about this game... and not so great parts. GREAT: - Visuals: Really pretty! I like the overall art style, character design, and customizable teahouse options. - Setting: Takes place in historical China and is pretty immersive with references in plot and in gameplay. - Story: Engaging and I'm invested. MC is likable, and so are the love interests and side characters. I'll keep playing this game to see how things progress. I hope the storyline doesn't end any time soon and keeps developing. - Gameplay: Typical merge game mechanics with multiple spawners, but so far, orders are well balanced and not all of them are super crazy to fulfill. Some orders can be completed within 100 stamina, others are more complex and require checking back in to reach higher level items. I haven't reached a wall yet, and I hope orders remain as a balanced mix. - Ad free! At least, in my experience so far. Please keep it that way 🙏 NOT GREAT: - Events: Steep time limits unless you pay for materials. And I have spent money on this game. But coupled with my hours of gameplay a day, I still don't think I'll complete some events. This makes the game just another pay to win merge game. Early rewards are fairly decent, but if you want better rewards and full completion, be prepared to pay. - Progress: As the story goes on, unlockable scenes get shorter and shorter. The option to choose furniture and decorations become less frequent. For example: You will finally have enough coins to continue the story -> the dialogue is essentially filler -> a little vase or decoration gets added without the option to choose what it is OR an old piece just gets cleared. In the beginning, I felt I had more opportunities to decorate the teahouse, but it's less often now. TL;DR: Fun game that I'll continue playing, but it relies on the same monetization tactics as many other merge games. To the devs: The core gameplay feels well-balanced with reasonable goals, but please consider applying that same balance to the limited-time events as well.

title: Favorite Gaming App I’ve ever played
body: This game is absolutely amazing! The story is fascinating and compelling, the merging is fun, the challenges are a bit tough but not impossible and even being an expert in both the fields of Tea and Textiles, I’ve learned so much about both fields! I was seriously taking notes when they were discussing dye methods! Qiu Wan is smart but not infallible and her generosity, wit and kindness is genuinely compelling. Not to mention I don’t think I’ve ever been so torn between romanceable characters before! All 3 of the male characters are interesting and different from each other, but they’re all likeable. There’s also a possible female romance which is so cool! Yuhuan is a great female character and I love her dynamic with Qiu Wan! I think we’re gonna need a harem ending lol I also love the new generator creator and storage system, it’s quite ingenious and so much better than all the other merge games I’ve played. A few notes: 1. I really wish that you could buy 100 energy for 10 gems twice a day rather than once. It feels like it runs out rather quickly. 2. We’ve had several times where characters have made it clear than they have feelings for our FL, and she just doesn’t respond. With her quick wit and keen eye of details, it seems impossible she doesn’t know. Maybe she’s just ignoring it but I feel like it would be more likely for her to face it head on and say something like: “I can’t return your feelings right now with my focus being wholly on the shops and avoiding the enemies at my doorstep.” That being said, I’d love to have options to pursue the various romances, so I hope the higher levels of affection scores have romance scenes! Thanks for all your hard work on this game! I love it!

title: Name Confusion
body: I love this game, it has such beautiful graphics and a very interesting storyline. Although I do not believe in reincarnation or any of the Chinese folklore as a Christian, I did grow up around it. I have one problem with this game so far and that is the name of the male servant. Wan has two permanent helpers in the Teahouse, a young girl and a young g man. The young man is initially named Zea but then further along in the story his name is suddenly changed to Ryen and then back to Zea. The name keeps changing randomly even though both names refer to the same character. This is not a first and last name situation either. I simply wanted to point the minor detail out. Otherwise, it is an outstanding game. The use of energy to produce matching objects helps gaming addicts like myself take a break, otherwise I would just keep matching until the game was over. There is also no getting stuck either if you fill the whole board. You simply have to delete a few pieces. I also like 2x production button where you can simply produce the next level of object instead of having to waste time producing the smallest object and merging all the way up. It saves space for when you have to merge to even higher level of objects. I really like this game and highly recommend it.

title: A merge game where I actually read the story??
body: I've played several merge games or other games that have these silly "storylines" you have to go through, and I ALWAYS skip as much as possible. This is the first one where the story is actually a little bit interesting! (Maybe I just watch too many period cdramas - that is what attracted me to this game!) I mean, it's not exactly high literature (or even a cheap beach read), and there have been a few bits I've skipped through, but there's just enough meat to keep me reading most entries. The game is also good about providing just enough extra energy packs and gems that I rarely (but not never) get frustrated. I've spent a few dollars so far, but if a game is basically held hostage until you keep paying I don't pay, I delete it. I've only spent money bc I like the game, I do think it's fairly well-balanced, and there are regular offers at prices I'm willing to pay. The one thing I would love is if there were a way to go back and change previous decorating choices - I'd like to be able to play with different combos rather than be stuck with something that it turns out doesn't look great with the next item. The decorating options are pretty limited as it is (but are at least all very pretty and well-designed), so a little more flexibility there would enhance that part of the game. A last note on the story: Sadly I think Qiu Wan should wind up with Tang Gan or Miss Noa instead of any of her male suitors, she has far more chemistry with them, but I doubt the developers are willing to go there.

Lastly, I love all the side challenges that keep the game extra fun and interesting. Thanks for developing such a great game- I feel so lucky to have discovered this gem!

title: Surpassed expectations!
body: I wasn’t expecting much when I downloaded this, I often play random games and delete them in a day, I’m so surprised with this one! The story is genuinely really engaging. The main character is so clever and it’s so fun to see her thoughts and for her to use her past life so strategically. Usually with the whole past life trope once the Mc gets revenge the brush over everything else, this game integrates it into the story really well! I found myself laughing a lot and the characters are genuinely so enjoyable! Really really fun. There are a few grammatical and spelling errors that take me out of the game a bit but nothing that makes it unreadable. If anything it catches me more off guard because everything is written fairly well. Some of the language also catches me off guard and I don’t know if this is a translation error or not. We’re in ancient china and the dialogue mostly reflects that until the Mc says smth like “get real!” Or her best friends says “girl!” Really pulls me out. Also, I’m not sure if some of the cutscene art for this is ai 😓 I might just be paranoid but I hope not, if it was I’d have to drop it. It seems like a lot of genuine passion was put into this game so itd really break my heart if the devs were to do something like this. And those are my only complaints! Incredible game, little to no ads, fun gameplay and story, I wish I had more energy so I could keep playing!! (Also, maybe add a log so people could go back to look at pervious stories or events? I’d love to go back and compare how Qui Wan grows!)
